Hey [~accountid:5d0c7ac70f1d390c4db46fed] , could this ticket be closed?

Looked into it a bit again, and the issue still seems to be related to Gatsby. The browser list in package.json and babelState.json seem to match, but the required polyfills are not defined there. 

I also checked the browsers supported by our current defined browser list, and even if it did correctly, the error we are seeing in the driver page happens on browsers that we would not support anyways.

A possible solution in the future if we want to support old browsers - define what browsers we want to support, create a list of required polyfill, and add all polyfills manually, but that is hard to maintain. 

For now, I’ve created a reminder to discuss this with the whole dev team when everyone is back.

Hey [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] 

Let me quickly explain the background of the performance calibrations. The reason why we set those up with P&C team is that we have a huge group of managers in CS and performance reviews always tend to have some extend of subjectiveness in them. Our goal is that people are evaluated fairly and managers have also additional support when it comes to doing these evaluations. 

No manager is expected to share any confidential details about anyone when filling in those sheets. It should be only the overall performance score together with overall summary of the performance. 

Only CS managers have access to these sheets and information on them. And there’s a clear expectation in place that this data cannot be shared outside of the group of managers. Meaning the access is already limited only to a number of people who need this data. Hope this clarifies it a bit further. 

Let me know if considering this we still need to hide the names - this is something we can absolutely do.

* Technical support has been dealing with the website domain since 2017, but due to the main CMS, Contentful, being owned by the Online Presence team now, we would like to hand over the domain to them. In general, we have 2 sub-domains within Website tickets: Terms & Conditions (T&C) and City and Operational change requests.
* T&C:
** T&C documents can be uploaded in two types:
*** PDF-file - can take from 2-5 minutes to upload per file
*** HTML version - can take from 20 to 40 minutes of editing in Contentful per document
** Use of a PDF or HTML version is determined by the Legal team - we default to uploading the PDF version, unless required otherwise
** The amount of tickets received doesn't always reflect the amount of work to be done
*** One SD request can ask for the upload of 1 PDF file -> 2-5 minutes of work
*** Another SD request can ask for changes in 10+ HTML files and uploads of new HTML files with linked new PDF documents inside -> half a day of work
* City and Operational Changes:
** City changes can include multiple factors
*** Vehicle category management on the city webpage
*** Prices & descriptions (most common requests)
*** Image handling
*** Category creation and archival
*** City launches
*** City description management, including new field creation requests
*** Other operational requests can include:
*** Country launches on the website
*** Language section management
** The amount of tickets received doesn't always reflect the amount of work to be done
*** One SD request can ask to change the price of one category in one city -> 2 minutes of work
*** Another SD request can ask for changes to category prices in all cities of a country -> 1-4 hours of work (e.g. Poland has requested changes to categories in all its cities once).
* There are also requests not currently managed by technical support:
** Updating FAQ and KB articles -> is done through Beehive and is managed by the CS Knowledge Management team
** Changing page layouts, changes on Blog pages, product webpages (e.g. scooters, rides, car-sharing, delivery or business) -> Online Presence
** More technical Contentful and code change requests -> Web dev team
** Driver & Fleet portals -> DriverX dev team
** Everything related to Delivery -> Delivery team

* [for Direction of change tooltip] - This specifies the direction that defines harmful changes e.g. “Not increase by more than” means that an increase by more than the specified MDE will be considered as harmful and be significant in scorecard.

*fraud_campaign_profile_by_device_uid*

{noformat}-- Get the activity of new users in the device for the last 30 days 
WITH device_user_camp AS (
SELECT etl.country_code, fud.user_id, fud.device_uid, DATEDIFF(day, uu.created_date, current_date) AS user_age
, SUM(CASE WHEN etl.created_date >= dateadd(day, -1, current_date) THEN (etl.bonus_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) else 0 END) AS total_disc_eur_1d
, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN etl.created_date >= dateadd(day, -1, current_date) THEN etl.order_id END) AS camp_events_1d
, SUM(CASE WHEN etl.created_date >= dateadd(day, -7, current_date) THEN (etl.bonus_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) else 0 END) AS total_disc_eur_7d
, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN etl.created_date >= dateadd(day, -7, current_date) THEN etl.order_id END) AS camp_events_7d
, SUM(etl.bonus_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) AS total_disc_eur_30d
, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(etl.order_id) AS camp_events_30d
FROM ng_public_spark.fraud_user_device AS fud 
JOIN ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
	ON (fud.user_id = etl.user_id)
JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu 
	ON (uu.id = fud.user_id)
WHERE true 
	AND etl.bonus_amount > 0
	AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
	AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
	AND etl.created_date >= dateadd(day, -30, current_date)
	AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created_date, current_date) <= 30
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
-- Get the amount of new users related to the device AND how many of them are deleted 
, device_deleted_users AS (
SELECT fud.device_uid, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(fud.user_id) AS device_total_users, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN uu.phone_anonymized = '0del' THEN uu.id END) AS deleted_users
FROM ng_public_spark.fraud_user_device AS fud 
JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu 
	ON (fud.user_id = uu.id)
GROUP BY 1
)
-- We calculate the features for the key 
, final_table AS (
SELECT duc.country_code || ':' || duc.device_uid AS key
, ddu.deleted_users AS count_deleted_users, ddu.device_total_users AS count_total_users
, (CAST(ddu.deleted_users AS double)/CAST(ddu.device_total_users AS double)) AS deleted_users_ratio
, SUM(duc.total_disc_eur_1d) AS sum_of_campaign_orders_1d, SUM(duc.camp_events_1d) AS count_of_campaign_orders_1d
, SUM(duc.total_disc_eur_7d) AS sum_of_campaign_orders_7d, SUM(duc.camp_events_7d) AS count_of_campaign_orders_7d
, SUM(duc.total_disc_eur_30d) AS sum_of_campaign_orders_30d, SUM(duc.camp_events_30d) AS count_of_campaign_orders_30d
FROM device_user_camp AS duc 
JOIN device_deleted_users AS ddu 
	ON (duc.device_uid = ddu.device_uid)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
-- Return the final results after filtering the 
SELECT f.key, f.count_total_users, f.count_deleted_users, f.deleted_users_ratio, f.count_of_campaign_orders_1d, f.count_of_campaign_orders_7d
, f.count_of_campaign_orders_30d, f.sum_of_campaign_orders_1d, f.sum_of_campaign_orders_7d, f.sum_of_campaign_orders_30d
FROM final_table as f
WHERE true 
	AND count_total_users >= 2{noformat}

{noformat}-- First, we obtain the users AND their respective creation-ip
WITH ips_and_users AS (
SELECT fu.user_id, fu.user_creation_ip, fu.created_date, uu.phone_anonymized
FROM ng_pii_spark.fraud_user AS  fu 
JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS  uu 
  ON (fu.user_id = uu.id)
WHERE true 
  AND fu.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -90, current_date)
  AND user_creation_ip IS NOT null 
)
-- We get the number of users created per day for each creatiON ip - We need for the further max we are going to do 
, created_per_day AS (
SELECT user_creation_ip, fu.created_date, approx_count_distinct(user_id) AS  count_created
, approx_count_distinct(CASE WHEN uu.phone_anonymized = '0del' THEN user_id END) AS  count_created_del
FROM ng_pii_spark.fraud_user AS  fu 
JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS  uu 
  ON (fu.user_id = uu.id)
WHERE true 
  AND fu.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -90, current_date)
  AND user_creation_ip IS NOT null
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2 DESC 
)
-- We get the campaign orders made per each creation-ip 
, ips_and_orders AS (
SELECT etl.country_code, etl.user_id, iu.user_creation_ip, etl.order_id, etl.order_type, etl.created_date, (etl.bonus_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) AS  bonus_amount_eur
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS  etl 
JOIN ips_and_users AS  iu 
  ON (iu.user_id = etl.user_id)
WHERE true 
  AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
  AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
  AND etl.bonus_amount > 0
  AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -15, current_date)
)
-- We calculate the user creatiON features for the ips 
, users_table AS (
SELECT cd.user_creation_ip
, SUM(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -1, current_date) THEN cd.count_created END) AS  count_users_created_1d
, SUM(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, current_date) THEN cd.count_created END) AS  count_users_created_7d
, SUM(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -15, current_date) THEN cd.count_created END) AS  count_users_created_15d
, SUM(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -1, current_date) THEN cd.count_created_del END) AS  count_users_deleted_1d
, SUM(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, current_date) THEN cd.count_created_del END) AS  count_users_deleted_7d
, SUM(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -15, current_date) THEN cd.count_created_del END) AS  count_users_deleted_15d
, max(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, current_date) THEN count_created else 0 END) AS  max_created_users_a_day_7d
, max(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -30, current_date) THEN count_created else 0 END) AS  max_created_users_a_day_30d
, max(CASE WHEN cd.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -90, current_date) THEN count_created else 0 END) AS  max_created_users_a_day_90d
FROM created_per_day AS  cd
GROUP BY 1
)
-- We calculate the order creatiON features for the ips 
, orders_table AS  (
SELECT io.country_code, io.user_creation_ip
, approx_count_distinct(CASE WHEN created_date >= DATEADD(day, -1, current_date) THEN io.order_id END) AS  count_of_campaign_orders_1d
, approx_count_distinct(CASE WHEN created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, current_date) THEN io.order_id END) AS  count_of_campaign_orders_7d
, approx_count_distinct(CASE WHEN created_date >= DATEADD(day, -15, current_date) THEN io.order_id END) AS  count_of_campaign_orders_15d
, SUM(CASE WHEN created_date >= DATEADD(day, -1, current_date) THEN io.bonus_amount_eur else 0 END) AS  amount_of_campaign_orders_1d
, SUM(CASE WHEN created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, current_date) THEN io.bonus_amount_eur else 0 END) AS  amount_of_campaign_orders_7d
, SUM(CASE WHEN created_date >= DATEADD(day, -15, current_date) THEN io.bonus_amount_eur else 0 END) AS  amount_of_campaign_orders_15d
FROM ips_and_orders AS  io 
GROUP BY 1,2
) 
-- We show the final results
SELECT ot.country_code || ':' || ot.user_creation_ip AS key
, count_users_created_1d, count_users_created_7d, count_users_created_15d
, count_users_deleted_1d, count_users_deleted_7d, count_users_deleted_15d
, max_created_users_a_day_7d, max_created_users_a_day_30d, max_created_users_a_day_90d
, count_of_campaign_orders_1d, count_of_campaign_orders_7d, count_of_campaign_orders_15d
, amount_of_campaign_orders_1d, amount_of_campaign_orders_7d, amount_of_campaign_orders_15d
FROM users_table AS  ut 
JOIN orders_table AS  ot 
  ON (ut.user_creation_ip = ot.user_creation_ip)
WHERE true 
-- We filter out the ips that don't have an interesting amount of created users 
  AND max_created_users_a_day_90d >= 5
  AND count_of_campaign_orders_15d > 0
  AND count_users_created_15d > 0{noformat}

Sharing [~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048]'s Privacy assessment:

*Background*: the contact details were collected at some point in the course of business dealings between Bolt managers and the city authorities for communication purpose. The email list was later compiled for further data processing by a third party (research / survey purpose). City officials do not know about this initiative. Some of these email addresses are public and some are not.
*Assessment*: I consider that further processing isn’t allowed without the explicit consent of the data subjects as the purpose is incompatible with the original purpose for which the data was processed.
*Recommendation*: Appropriate consent must first be obtained from data subjects. Once the the survey has been conducted, Bolt must also ensure that we have processes in place to allow us to respect the individual's right to request access to personal data collected by Deloitte’s survey. We must be prepared to facilitate requests not only for access, but also for deletion of personal information upon request.

I analysed about 20-30 crashlytics reports with HTTP timeout and it seems that in the majority of the cases the app is in the background and have limited access to make network requests or there are other HTTP requests failed as well (eg. fetching payment information or polling). Almost in every case there is log that MQTT connection is interrupted as well. Considering all of this I suppose HTTP timeout is a normal response and nothing serious happening. Besides if MQTT connection is interrupted, there will be an attempt to restore this connection and when it is re-established a new attempt to obtain currently active chats and to sync chat history will be made, so the chat will stay consistent.

I lowered the severity of the log message to INFO so it won’t pollute the crashlytics board.

# Clause 2 of section 6 (Liability) was significantly amended as follows: "_The_ *-_total aggregate_-* _liability of Bolt_ *-_for all the claims arising under or_-* _in connection with_ *-_the Agreement during the period of one calendar year, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise shall be limited to the amounts paid_-* _any loss or damage that Customer may incur as a result of using Bolt Business shall be equal to the actual amount received by Bolt from_ *_the_* _Customer_ *-_to Bolt_-* _under the Agreement in the_ *-_3_-*_6 month_*_s_* *-_period prior to_-* *_preceding_* _the date_ *-_the first_-* *_on which the_* _claim arose._". This change expands Bolt's liability in terms of cause of the claim (previously these were only claims in connection to the Agreement) and also increases the amount Bolt will be liable to pay (6 months' pay instead of 3). This change should probably be rejected or at least it requires an approval. Official position according to the [Playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923659743/Contracting+playbook+for+Bolt+s+General+Business+Portal+T+C.+Team+Account+Ride+Booker.+Standard+Customers] is as follows: "_Bolt Business and Bolt Services are provided on an "as is" and “as available” basis. Bolt does not guarantee that access shall be uninterrupted or error free. Hence the possibility of submitting any successful claims against Bolt is very low. While we work relentlessly to maximize Customer satisfaction with our services you remain free to use competitive services, and are free to stop using Bolt services at any time without sanctions._"
# Customer deleted clause 6.3 of the original [Special Terms|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LQeTeDuZJP_rwZ8WNIF0mN4UflhpFeFxt1xZbmxtYtA/edit]. However, they added this wording to clause 3 of section 6 (Liability): "_Bolt shall not be liable for any costs, losses or damages caused due to inaccurate or incomplete data provided by Customer, nor shall Bolt be liable for the actions, errors or omissions of driver, courier or other independent user of Bolt Services."_. This wording is not protecting Bolt well enough and this should not be acceptable. We would like to add the original wording.
# Customer replaced Bolt Services to Bolt Business in clause 3 of section 6 (Liability): "_..or other unlawful activity connected to the User's use of_ *_Bolt Business_*_._". Technically Users are not using Bolt Business, they are using Bolt Services. It is the Customer who is the user of Bolt Business. Therefore this change should also be rejected.
# Customer deleted clause 6.7 of the original [Special Terms|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LQeTeDuZJP_rwZ8WNIF0mN4UflhpFeFxt1xZbmxtYtA/edit]. This is our precaution in case of a conflict between what is stated in the agreement and in the applicable law. We would like to keep the wording "_The limitations of liability set out in this clause shall apply to the maximum extent permitted by law._" in the agreement.
# Customer requested to remove the following wording from clause 4 of section 7 (Term and termination): "_Confidentiality provisions shall terminate in 5 years from the end of the Agreement._". They say that they see no reason for that, but by removing this wording and not amending the first clause confidentiality obligations would remain permanent, which is not acceptable. According to the [Playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923659743/Contracting+playbook+for+Bolt+s+General+Business+Portal+T+C.+Team+Account+Ride+Booker.+Standard+Customers] we can agree to the following alternative wording: "_All outstanding payment obligations, as well as obligations arising out of liability provisions of this Agreement shall survive the termination of this Agreement. The confidentiality obligations of the Parties shall expire upon termination of the Agreement, with the exception of those confidentiality obligations imposed by the applicable data protection laws._".
# Customer suggested to amend clause 5 of section 8 (Final provisions) so as neither party would be able to assign its rights or obligations under the agreement to any third party. For some reason the wording in this template differs from the wording used in clause 8.5 of the original [Special Terms|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LQeTeDuZJP_rwZ8WNIF0mN4UflhpFeFxt1xZbmxtYtA/edit]. In any case, we would like to be able to assign agreement automatically should such need arise. Therefore, our preferred wording would be this: "_This Agreement and the rights and obligations thereunder may not be assigned or transferred to third parties by the Customer, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of Bolt. Agreement may be assigned and transferred by Bolt, in whole or in part, in Bolt’s sole discretion provided that the assignee is not a direct competitor of the Customer and has assumed the obligations under the Agreement._". In case the Customer does not agree, then subject to approval by the Regional Head of Sales we can agree to amend the wording of this clause as follows: "_This Agreement may not be assigned by either party, in whole or in part, without the prior consent of the other party. A party may assign the Agreement without such consent, but with notice to the other party, in connection with a merger or a sale of all of its equity or assets._".
# Customer suggested adding the following wording to clause 6 of section 8 (Final provisions): "_McDonald's contractual standards forming Annex No. 1 of this Agreement are an integral part of this Agreement, which Bolt hereby undertakes to comply with_". We can agree to this, but the special terms need to be signed according to which the set of terms included in the special terms would take priority over anything regulated in Customer documentation as per [Contracting Playbook for Tier 1 Customers|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923561494/Contracting+playbook.+Team+Account+Ride+Booker.+Tier+1+Customers] - suggested additional wording in this respect. Here are the main issues identified in connection to this annex they suggested:
## "_Subcontracting of services to be provided by the Supplier or delegation of their duties without the McDonald’s express written consent, unless otherwise agreed in the agreement;_" - we need to add a note that for the sake of clarity Bolt is not offering transportation services and transportation service providers are independent third parties and not Bolt’s subcontractors.
## "_Assignment of the Supplier’s right to receive payment from McDonald’s to a third party or to accounts maintained in a third country;_ " - this should create no problems as long as we will extend the meaning of Supplier to include Bolt’s group companies in regards to this particular point. This will help us to reorganise business in CZ and SK if necessary.
## "_The Supplier or any other party entering into an agreement on behalf of the Supplier declares that, to the best of its knowledge, no person directly or indirectly linked to it is an agent, an employee, a supplier, a licence user or an officer of McDonald’s or any of McDonald’s subsidiary, associated company or parent company. The Parties to this agreement acknowledge that this representation is one of the incentives to conclude this agreement, that McDonald’s rely on this representation, and that any deceptive conduct will be reason for withdrawal from this agreement by McDonald’s._" - we need to add a note that for the sake of clarity Bolt does not consider drivers and couriers to be directly or indirectly connected to Bolt and drivers and couriers can be employees of McDonald's. Drivers and couriers are not suppliers and are not parties to this Agreement.

They also specify that personal data processing related to obligations of Bolt shall be determined by the laws of Estonia which is fine for us.
# Customer added the following additional wording to clause 9 of section 8 (Final provisions): "_This Agreement has been drawn up in the Czech and English languages. The Parties declare that they understand the contents of the Contract and undertake to abide by its contents._". We can agree to this.

With that out of the way, the General Data Protection Regulation requires a proper legal basis to justify each case of data processing / data transferring. At the same time, personal data must be strictly limited to the minimum amount of personal data that the operator needs to provide the service.

If Bolt provides full platform services to the operator, the only legal basis for the exchange of personal data will be the legal obligations of the operator to receive and maintain certain data. However, this will depend on local regulations in each jurisdiction. I would advise to involve local legal counsel to:

* know if the operator is obligated by law to maintain access to certain personal data;
* the exact scope of that personal data; and
* if Bolt can act as a point of contact with the authorities in cases of incident reporting.

Also, after reviewing section 2.4, I have the following concerns:

* the list of personal data is somewhat extensive. The operator did not provide any explanation/justification why they need this data;
* ‘_to be used for customer care purposes_' - this is very broad and can include marketing, we do not want that. Also, it seems that Bolt would be responsible for pre- and post- ride customer support. So I don't understand what exactly the operator means by customer care.

Please be aware that we should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Nb: the end of the financial year is 31ts December.

The deadline for presentation of the annual accounts is within the month following the date of their approval by the General Meeting, i.e. the final day must coincide with the last day of the month following the month in which they were approved. *Retrospective on creating an updated process*

* Analyzing the data on a market level was useful because it allowed me to identify some positive and negative outliers which led to adjusting the process:
** It was found that markets that call drivers instead of messaging them have higher CSAT, so this step was implemented in the global process.
** NO-specific instructions were removed because they weren’t useful in any way.
* I’ve got a lot of useful feedback from TLs, so it’s definitely useful to engage them in such projects.
** For example, one TL pointed out that we should call riders once we get an update from the driver to speed up the resolution and it was added to the global process.
* Reviewing some actual cases also proved to be useful as it enabled me to improve the process further.
* It was interesting to compare some process data in the old and new process (e.g. total number of steps, the number of value-adding steps etc.) because it gave me some understanding of how much the process has been improved.

Hi [~accountid:627a6caf23d61e006fc44e83],

Thank you for sharing the idea! I'll provide you with a few remarks, but I don’t think there is an option for us to have accurate and consistent location data at the moment.

First of all, some of the events are continuous by their nature. It means that it’s not really connected to a specific location much. A simple example is {{Driver Speeding}}.

Furthermore, some of the events already imply *when* the event has happened. For instance, {{Driver Contacting Rider After Journey}}. Or, {{Driver Refuses Assistance Animal}}. This can be indirectly retrieved from the order’s data as well (canceled orders, far from drop off).

If we go with clarifying more precise location details for certain events, for instance, {{Significant}} ones, it might still be unreasonable. Sometimes it is not too appropriate to ask where the event has happened; it might as well raise some additional privacy concerns. 

Finally, if we ask for a specific location, we’d need to have the coordinates to have it visualised. If we use *address fields* instead, it creates a significant amount of extra work for an agent to fill out, hence the odds of human error. If we ask or assume the *approximate timing* (such as *before, during, or after the journey*), we don’t really get any valuable input for maps either (except for verifying the data that we get on pick-up and drop-off locations).

Interpreting something like *EFR per km²* would be also quite challenging in my opinion, as the events are not distributed evenly on the ground. For instance, there might be 1 km² with only one drivable road, where 10 events happened in a certain point; or 1 km² with 10 roads and one event happening on each of them. The numbers are the same, but the patterns are different. Also, what would be the polygons to get this calculated?

Please, let me know what you think and if maybe you envision something more specific.

Hey [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] ! 

Thank you for sharing your concerns. I agree that the proposed solution is not ideal as we are interfering with the provision of services limiting the choice for passengers and drivers. However, looking at this from the practical perspective:

* the likelihood seems small that passengers would pick the Basic category that is significantly more expensive than Bolt even if the offer is there. Thus, in practice drivers most probably will not lose many customers as a result of the introduction of this “hidden” feature. But I absolutely agree with [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] that there might be exceptions when users are ready to pay more for the lower category if a vehicle is in near proximity and a user is in a rush.
* if would be very difficult to claim that we are technically intervening unless the information is leaked and/or labour authorities start auditing us specifically in relation to the pricing and offers displayed on the app.
* How notable would be the change from the driver's perspective? Will drivers notice a rapid decrease in orders? This is for businesses to assess [~accountid:712020:c0cc6249-3a02-4388-bba0-7e8370980ebe]. 
** If the rapid decrease in order will not take place, the likelihood that drivers will become angry and claim that Bolt is intervening is minor. 
** If changes could be substantial, this can mark the start of unpleasant consequences if drivers get really angry and, for example, submit a claim to Labour inspection or even the court that Bolt is excessively intervening in and supervising the provision of services, thus, is acting as an employer.

Considering the above, I would tolerate introduction of such feature (at least until there is a better solution) provided (i) the feature is not applicable to orders where higher price for Basic could be reasonably justified and (ii) it would not substantially affect the current order display making drivers suspicious.

For example:

# Orders that should stay visible (to allow riders to take more expensive but desirable ride, if they prefer so)  
## EUR 5 Bolt vehicle that is 10 min away from the rider (visible)
## EUR 8 Basic vehicles that is 3 min away from the rider (visible)
# Order that could be hidden 
## EUR 5 Bolt vehicle that is 3 min away from the rider (visible)
## EUR 8 Basic vehicles that is 10 min away from the rider or EUR 8 Basic vehicle that is 3 min away (just as Bolt vehicle) (hidden)

If this feature is implemented, it's crucial to monitor its impact on demand and supply to prevent a situation where high demand outpaces the available supply, leading to frustration and user dissatisfaction. 

*Alternatively,* [~accountid:639329def48fbd9b62da5e03] is it possible to implement a pricing algorithm that adjusts the prices? That is, if the price of the Basic category becomes higher than the price for the Bolt without valid reasons, the algorithm can automatically increase the price for the Bolt  ride. This approach would allow to regulate prices without the need to hide rides or intervene in demand and supply dynamics.

The query below will do the backfilling “magic”:


{code:sql}select a.days,
       a.last_update,
       a.expires_at,
       CONCAT('UPDATE business_company_promo_code SET expires_at = \'', a.expires_at, '\' WHERE id = ',
              a.bcpc_id) as update_query
from (
         select bcpc.id                           as                                       bcpc_id,
                JSON_EXTRACT(bpc.rules, '$.days') as                                       days,
                bcpc.last_update,
                DATE_ADD(bcpc.last_update, INTERVAL JSON_EXTRACT(bpc.rules, '$.days') DAY) expires_at
         from business_company_promo_code bcpc
                  inner join business_promo_code bpc on bcpc.promo_code_id = bpc.id
         where bcpc.state = 'active' and bcpc.expires_at is null
     ) a;{code}

Hey [~accountid:5b7beb0fc5e21441d0929c5c]!

From the privacy POV, if the driver/other users request an account deletion, we should delete their data from our systems in full, except some info that we need for accounting and fraud prevention purposes. We state this on our privacy policies as well. 

If the user requests their account to be restored, we should ask the driver/other user to go through the sign-up process anew since we don’t have their data in our systems. I appreciate we have some pieces of information once the account is deleted, nut we shouldn’t have this in our systems and we are working on our data retention procedures at Bolt. 

*To sum up:*
1. We *should not restore* their accounts once these accounts are deleted.
2. Instead, we should ask the user to sign up in the app and go through the sign up process one more time. 
3. If there is a pushback from users/drivers, we can think of a solution of asking them before the account deletion, if they want us to retain their data in our systems (only storage) for 1 year (for example) in case they change their mind and decide to restore an account. But this process should be created and evaluated from legal and privacy sides as well.

Hi again Anastasia, 

I have now taken a closer look at this issue, please see below. 

On a general note, Bolt are required to have some sort of CS available for three years after making a delivery, as people who have made orders are technically entitled to submit complaints to Bolt about the delivery/delivered goods during this time. In my opinion, this requirement is fulfilled by Bolt keeping the possibility of sending an _email_ to contact CS - i.e. even if the support function in the app is closed. Therefore, I see no obstacles from a legal perspective that would prevent us from closing the support function at this point. 

It should be mentioned that complaints must be submitted by people who have made orders no later than two months from discovering any defect in the delivery/delivered goods. Given that it has already been two months since delivery closed in Sweden and the CS function has been left open, I think the risk of receiving further CS matters from customers is quite small.

In summary, from a legal perspective, please feel free to close the CS support function for deliveries.

h3. {color:#36b37e}*Data analysis insights*{color}

h4. *Handling time* _(5 min)_

* AHT is within the target (<8min) in all markets.
* The lowest AHT is in Partner markets - Austria, Georgia, Mexico, and Saudi Arabia (avg. 1.7 min)
** They don’t follow the process and make quick refunds (examples [1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/244728756], [2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/248390553], [3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/240498467]).
* Within the Core markets, the AHT is the lowest in PL 3.3 min, UA 3.4 min, and PT 3.8 min.
** All markets have high PA scores - PL 90.5%, UA 92.4%, PT 92.7% PA in May.
** The process for unconfirmed cases is short and concise, also these markets use macros, thus many cases are closed very quickly (examples [1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/243259649], [2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/250818440]). Yet in some cases, the quick decision that the case is unconfirmed results in low CSAT.

h4. *CSAT* _(80.2%)_ & Process DSATs _(61.01%)_

* CSAT is low for unconfirmed cases when the ride happened and pickup and destination points did not change. Overall, while reviewing the tickets I saw a lot of false claims and it looks like quite often riders this way are trying to avoid paying for rides. Low CSAT here is inevitable, as otherwise, we would be making a lot of unnecessary refunds (examples [1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/246893625], [2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/240744040], [3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/240798791]).
* Some markets are using different, not documented methods to confirm the case, e.g. in France, they are asking for pictures or receipts that would prove that the rider was somewhere else when the ride took place ([example|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/251982718]). {color:#bf2600}_The part of the process for confirming the case should be improved_{color}.

h4. *SSAT* _(59.8%)_

* Looking at the same examples as for the CSAT (examples [1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/246893625], [2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/240744040], [3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/240798791]) it is visible that cases are not closed after a first solution because riders are trying to get a refund.
* Also, since BB is the refund method indicated in the process, some riders do not agree with that and reopen the case by asking for a refund to the original payment method ([example|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/241143590]). 
* {color:#bf2600}_Clarify the refund possibilities in the process._{color}

Hi again Anastasia,

I have now taken a closer look at this issue, please see below.

On a general note, Bolt is required to have some sort of CS available for three (3) years after making a delivery, as people who have made orders are technically entitled to submit complaints to Bolt about the delivery/delivered goods during this time. In my opinion, this requirement is fulfilled by Bolt keeping the possibility of sending an _email_ to contact CS - i.e. even if the support function in the app is closed. Therefore, I see no obstacles from a legal perspective that would prevent us from closing the support function at this point.

It should be mentioned that complaints must be submitted by people who have made orders no later than two (2) months from discovering any defect in the delivery/delivered goods. Given that it has already been two months since delivery closed in Sweden and the CS function has been left open, I think the risk of receiving further CS matters from customers is quite small.

Furthermore, it should be mentioned that CS needs to map-out and formalise ongoing disputes and claims in order to ensure that these are closed before the CS function in the app is closed. If there are still ongoing discussions between customers and CS then please ensure that these discussions are moved to another medium so that the customer can be ensured that we are dealing with their matter. For example, CS could inform that the CS function will be closed down and that we will continue to support their matter via email.

In summary, from a legal perspective, please feel free to close the CS support function for deliveries while keeping the above in mind. Please let us know if you have any further questions or if we can close the ticket.

Best,

Ida

+*Summary of call with Lavin on new feature*+

* From riders perspective - when the passenger is in the vehicle and the passenger feels unsafe they can record the journey. 
* From drivers perspective - when the driver feels threatened/unsafe they can initiate the recording. 
* There is no necessity to roll out the feature if there is a legal/privacy risk. 

+*AB Summary of new feature*+ 

# Has the UK Privacy Team signed off on all privacy aspects of this feature? 
# Does both the passenger and driver need to consent beforehand (prior to accepting the trip) to be recorded? 
# What happens if the passengers consents to the recording or the trip but the driver refuses? vice-versa can the person who wants the trip recorded proceed with the recording? 
# What happens in the event that there is a dispute?, how would the driver/passenger access the recording? would Bolt be intervening in such disputes and provide the complainant with the recording? what consents are in place surrounding this? My concerns here is Bolt as standard business practice does not get involved in disputes between passengers and drivers, however if Bolt are in possession of the recording Bolt may be compelled to provide this recording if a SAR’s request is made by either party, Bolt does not want to get bogged down with such requests as passengers and drivers can regularly disagree on matters and we may potentially open up the floodgate to requests of the recording. 
# Will the driver and passenger provide their consent by conduct i.e. the passenger consents when the passenger enters the vehicle, the driver consents when the driver accepts the booking. 

To summarise and as discussed during our call, I think it is best that the privacy team review all privacy aspects of rolling out this new feature, if the privacy team feel that this can be rolled out legal and privacy can work together on how consent can be obtained, legal can then determine and assess whether an update on the T&C’s are required.

For purposes of your discussion tomorrow, my thoughts are:

* *Is Bliq compliant with privacy laws?* - Based on a review of their website privacy notice, Bliq appears to be in breach of its transparency obligations under A13/14 of the GDPR. This is because their [Privacy Notice|https://www.bliq.app/en-privacy] does not clearly state what categories of personal data are being processed, for what purpose(s), about which categories of individual(s) and on what legal bases. They would be required to provide information via a privacy notice(s) about how they process: (i) drivers' personal data when the drivers' use the app, and (ii) riders' personal data they process via their app in order to facilitate the service to the driver. The notice to the driver should be provided when they sign up to the app and the notice to the riders should be provided at the latest within 1 month of receiving the rider personal data (as they don't receive that data directly from the rider).
* *Could we report Bliq to the German Data Protection Authorities and what evidence would be required?* - In theory, yes - we would need to confirm if there is a specific process we would need to follow. I have asked Markus (DPO Team) to check and will let you know asap. In terms of evidence, I suspect we would just need to link a copy of the website and summarise our concerns.
* *Should we report Bliq to the Germany Data Protection Authorities? What could be the potential impact/fallout for us?* - The regulator will expect us to have a document which sets out the technical data flows (which I don't think we have) so they can understand how the data flows between our app and Bliq's app. This would inadvertently open us up to scrutiny from the regulator about our personal data processes and our level of compliance which is not in line with legal requirements. In particular, the most obvious area of non-compliance is our own privacy notices which are not sufficient - that is why we have prioritised a review/update of them this year to align them with legal requirements. The process of updating our notices is due to be completed by the end of the year.
* *Next steps?* - If Markus/JK want to pursue the privacy angle then we can prioritise the review/update of our notices to prevent any unwanted attention on our own data protection compliance position but would need to re-allocate resources within the team and divert away from Q3 MVRA priority projects. {quote}What are the business needs this fills compared to what we have at the moment?{quote}

Few weeks ago we received automated email from Apple that our iOS Rider app has exceeded 200MB for one of its bundle size. This means that users will not be able to download/update to it automatically when they are on cellular network. This will have negative effect on acquiring new customers, especially in markets where cellular network speeds are lower and bandwidth is expensive.

In order to understand where our app bundle size is spent, we need insights. And in addition to being able to investigate current state of the app bundle, we want to have continuous monitoring of it.
Emerge Size Analysis ([https://www.emergetools.com/product/sizeanalysis)|https://www.emergetools.com/product/sizeanalysis)] allows all that:

# Breakdown of size in frameworks (SDK)s. Allow us to see how much we spend on external SDKs, eg. Veriff, GoogleMaps, ...
# Breakdown of size in types of resources. Allows us to see if there is abnormally large resources. Eg. we saw that just the translations in our app are 5% of whole app size.
# Insights how to reduce the app size. Some of those approaches we were aware but we had no idea what the effect will be without trying. At the moment we can immediately see how much we could save if we invested time into implementing some of them, and also where it will not pay off.

This part of the tool works on compiled version of our app and they will not have access to our source code.
They did already upload our AppStore version and we can get demo version insights here: [https://www.emergetools.com/app/example/ios/ee.mtakso.client?buildContent=insights|https://www.emergetools.com/app/example/ios/ee.mtakso.client?buildContent=insights|smart-link] 

Next steps would be to also try out their Performance Analysis suite [https://docs.emergetools.com/docs/performance-testing|https://docs.emergetools.com/docs/performance-testing)] to make sure we don't have regressions in app launch time, and Launch Booster [https://docs.emergetools.com/docs/launch-booster-ios|https://docs.emergetools.com/docs/launch-booster-ios)] to increase app launch speed.

In order to make sure that there are no regressions, we want to integrate it into our Pull Request workflow. This will allow us to catch any regressions before they get merged and we can pinpoint what kind of changes cause our app to increase in size or to become slow.

h2. All fields in {{WHERE}} clause are covered by the index

There’s no difference in the performance of two indices when all the columns in {{WHERE}} clause are covered by it.

h2. Not all fields in index are present in the query

In this case performance depends on which exact fields are used in the {{WHERE}} clause.
If we omit fields that come first then performance degrades real quick. 

However, let’s consider following query:

{code:sql}SELECT * from a/b WHERE domain = 'rides_and_rental' AND id = 12358173;{code}

For low-cardinality-first index we get worse performance and scan 5232284.39 rows:

{noformat}+--------------------+----------+---------+----------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|id                  |estRows   |task     |access object                           |operator info                                                  |
+--------------------+----------+---------+----------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|IndexReader_7       |0.30      |root     |                                        |index:Selection_6                                              |
|└─Selection_6       |0.30      |cop[tikv]|                                        |eq(index_test_local.a.id, 12358173)                            |
|  └─IndexRangeScan_5|5232284.39|cop[tikv]|table:a, index:idx(domain, group_id, id)|range:["rides_and_rental","rides_and_rental"], keep order:false|
+--------------------+----------+---------+----------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------+{noformat}

For high cardinality the TiDB is able to pinpoint a particular record:

{noformat}+-------------+-------+----+-------------+-------------------------------------------------+
|id           |estRows|task|access object|operator info                                    |
+-------------+-------+----+-------------+-------------------------------------------------+
|Selection_6  |0.30   |root|             |eq(index_test_local.b.domain, "rides_and_rental")|
|└─Point_Get_5|1.00   |root|table:b      |handle:12358173                                  |
+-------------+-------+----+-------------+-------------------------------------------------+{noformat}

h2. Conclusion

Index selection should be based on a particular use-case

Hi [~accountid:61386b11a4f86e0069546dff],

The Product Legal team has conducted a global assessment of this feature and it has been determined that no additional local review is required from a legal perspective other than the privacy review. I have created a sub-ticket for the privacy team to conduct their review and [~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] will get back to you on that matter. 

Regarding NO specifically I still did a sanity-check of the Norwegian criminal code which includes the following wording on this topic: 

h4. *_§ 205.Krenkelse av retten til privat kommunikasjon_*

_Med bot eller fengsel inntil 2 år straffes den som uberettiget_

_a. og ved bruk av teknisk hjelpemiddel hemmelig avlytter eller gjør_ +*_hemmelig opptak_*+ _av telefonsamtale eller annen_ +*_kommunikasjon mellom andre_*+_, eller av forhandlinger i lukket møte som han ikke selv deltar i, eller som han uberettiget har skaffet seg tilgang til,_

There are several factors that need to be fulfilled in order for this section to apply to the audio trip recording. Since either the rider or driver actively needs to activate the feature in the app we deem that it is not classified as Bolt recording a conversation between other parties, rather it should be seen as the driver or rider recording a conversation in which they participate. Such a scenario is not regulated in the Norwegian criminal code and Norwegian criminal law is based on the principle that you can only be punished for actions that are directly regulated in a criminal code. Hence, we have assessed that the audio trip recording does not fall within the prohibition in § 205. 

However, please note that there is a risk that a court would make a different assessment but we deem this to be a low and rather theoretical risk and the Legal team has therefore determined that the feature can be rolled out in Norway (*pending approval from privacy)*. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

I understand that you have already received the approval from privacy to roll out the feature as planned.

Regarding SE specifically the Swedish criminal code includes the following wording on this topic: 

h4. _4 kap. 9 a §_

_Den som i annat fall än som sägs i 8 §_ +*_olovligen_*+ _medelst tekniskt hjälpmedel för återgivning av ljud i hemlighet avlyssnar eller_ +*_upptager tal_*+ _i enrum, samtal_ +*_mellan andra_*+ _eller förhandlingar vid sammanträde eller annan sammankomst, vartill allmänheten icke äger tillträde och_ +*_som han själv icke deltager i_*+ _eller som han obehörigen berett sig tillträde till, dömes för olovlig avlyssning till böter eller fängelse i högst två år._ 

There are several factors that need to be fulfilled in order for this section to apply to the audio trip recording which have been underlined above. The key factor is that it needs to be a recording between parties where the recording party does not participate. Since either the rider or driver actively needs to activate the feature in the app we deem that it is not classified as Bolt recording a conversation between other parties, rather it should be seen as the driver or rider recording a conversation in which they participate. Such a scenario is not regulated in the Swedish criminal code and Swedish criminal law is based on the principle that you can only be punished for actions that are directly regulated in a criminal code. Hence, we have assessed that the audio trip recording does not fall within the prohibition in _4 kap. 9 a §_. 

However, please note that there is a loophole where it potentially could be argued that Bolt is the recording party since the recording is completed within the Bolt app and the parties of the conversation do not have access to the actual recording (while Bolt could get access if a ticket is raised). Hence, there is risk that a court would make a different assessment than what Bolt did globally but we deem this to be a low and rather theoretical risk and the Legal team has therefore determined that the feature can be rolled out in Sweden from a legal perspective. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Thank you [~accountid:6052891a695c3900706cc743] for the additional context. 

We always try to avoid mutable information in our content. If the cancellation fee for NL would change, we would have to update the content manually to reflect that - and if we weren’t informed or didn’t notice that it changed riders might contact us (understandably so) to complain about a higher-than-expected cancellation fee. 

Since we operate in so many markets, we have content for each and every market, often in 2-3 different languages per market. We currently don’t state the specific cancellation fees for any markets in similar articles. 

If we know that this information (cancellation fee amount in this case) does not change or does not change often (more than yearly) AND we consider it a big pain point for customers, we could consider including this in self-help content. This would include a lot of manual work for changing and up-keeping the content, which is why we would rather not include this type of information in the content.



I think there are a few other things to explore though, before deciding on any actions here:

# How do riders see the cancellation fee amount currently? Do they get a pop-up or is it written somewhere that they will/might be charged the 27 EUR (why is the CF so high? 😮 )
# Can we consider a product solution? Even if we were to include this in the self-help, I think that most users won’t check this specific article before canceling a ride - Either way, it’s a better user experience to get a very clear pop-up message saying “if you cancel now, you will pay XX EUR” rather than relying on self-help



Curious to hear your thoughts on the last points - And if you have some example cases (beehive URLs) of this scenario, please also send those along with some data (even if estimated numbers) on this issue.

Thanks!

* At some point we discussed a similar thing with Sten Suitsev but according to him, rider rating takes into account not only the behaviour pertaining to drivers. Rider might rate the trip poorly because the platform was not functioning properly or the price was too high etc. These are not issues driver can fix.
* Are we going to issue some warnings to the drivers before imposing a block?
* With Driver Score (the implementation of which is also imperfect from reclass perspective) drivers at least see the score and can adjust their behaviour. Removing drivers from our platform based on riders' rating is not a bad feature from reclass perspective per se - in the case of this feature we would be able to claim in court that rider is in control of driver quality, not Bolt. However, my understanding from Product Global perspective was that we don’t want to move in this direction.

All in all, just fyi - there is a big reclass defence strategy project going on where we are trying to fix or invent new features that would work both from Product and Legal perspective.

Hello!
I also am not aware of such option being used by other businesses.

Our current design *does not* include the possibility to opt-out from the pixel tracking (all data tracking will be conducted by Amazon, we will simply save the provided data at our end).

We could potentially let the user to "opt-out” (e.g. by clicking into specific link in the email message) by simply *not* *saving* the data which Amazon sends to us. Such approach would have two main downsides:

* We would most likely need to include the brief description of “what is pixel tracking and where to opt-out” in every email. Personally, I have never seen something like this in any email which uses pixel tracking, so it might look unusual/worrying from the user point of view.
* We would not have a simple way to opt-in again. Once a user opt-outs, we would loose him/her forever from our deliverability statistics 😄

*Advantages of the new feature*

* It encourages drivers to take trips that may initially not seem worth it, however once the pricing is slightly increased this may give the driver an incentive to take the journey. 

*Disadvantages of the new feature*

* It may have a negative affect on drivers declining trips more regularly in the hope that the rider will opt for the increased price as this would be more beneficial to the driver. 
* This feature could potentially deter passengers away from using the Bolt Platform, if riders regularly have difficulties getting a driver on the original price and are only able to get a driver at the increased price, riders may then be swayed to checking other ride hailing apps to compare prices (although this may be something that riders are already doing when deciding to order a ride). 

*Is a terms and conditions update required*

* [~accountid:6242fffc1da0e10071388193] asked the GFT slack channel if any other countries have rolled out this feature and whether a T&Cs update was required, the response in the chat was that none of the other teams have rolled this feature out. 
* As this will have an impact on both the driver and the passengers experience when using the Bolt Platform I think the T&Cs will need to be updated to incorporate an explanation on the price increase and the rational behind it. 
* I have looked at the current driver and passenger terms and conditions and do not feel that any of the clauses currently address this fluctuation in pricing. In the passenger T&Cs the section ‘other costs’ outlines cancellation, wait time and cleaning fees, I do not feel that this section addresses this feature. Moreover, in the driver T&Cs it outlines dynamic pricing and minimum expected journey fee, I do not think that this clause addresses this feature either. 

*Are there any reclassification risks*

* There are no controls placed onto the driver with this new feature, this feature actually gives the driver more control to decline / accept journeys the driver wishes to take. I do not see any red flags here which would give rise to a re-classification risk.

*Risks* 

I cannot see any significant risks rolling out this new feature, it is common for passengers to shop around so I do not think this feature will act as a huge deterrent for passengers using the Bolt platform. 

*Sign offs* 

To check with [~accountid:62a057be6a7b750068a28b0b] if all relevant sign offs for this feature have taken place. 

*Summary*

[~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3] to discuss this new feature with [~accountid:5fc110f647ac91006fc4977a] for a steer on whether this feature needs a T&Cs up-date and if it can be rolled out with low risks.

Hi [~accountid:5b8d306bfa38ae2c89608b95] as discussed today, the outside attorney clarified that the new pricing experiment does not directly result in liability for criminal offenses and/or administrative offenses from a consumer law and competition law perspective provided the rules mentioned below are taken into due consideration. 

It appears to me that the testing would not affect the rules below and the only pending question that was raised is whether or not the data resulting from the test will be anonymous or not? Could you please confirm? 

* *PRICING DISPLAY*
** The product must display the exact selling price in Euro that the consumer will pay (including all taxes).
** In some cases, the price of the unit of measurement (price per litre, for example) must be also displayed. 
** The price must be displayed next to the corresponding product in a way that is visible, unambiguous, and perfectly legible for the consumer.

{color:#36b37e}CATARINA: In my understanding the test will not affect the pricing display.{color}

* *PRICING VARIATIONS*
** If the pricing variation is positive (the good is more expensive than before), there is no specific  information obligation
** If the price variation is negative ( incorporating a discount or promotion), the seller has the obligation of displaying the discounted/promoted price and the previous lowest price (i.e., the lowest price at which the product was sold in the last 30 days) next to the product.

{color:#36b37e}CATARINA: In my understanding the test will involve a negative variation for some clients and therefore there is the obligation of displaying as well the previous lowest price. This is something we had already discussed and noted by HQ that must be complied with.{color}

* *USE OF DYNAMIC PRICE ALGORITHM*
** Retailers can use algorithms to track the client’s online browsing behaviour preferences and to set prices according the demand dynamics (airlines and hotels are particularly savvy in this regard).
** Before making a purchase, the client must be informed by Bolt that a personalised pricing algorithm is being used. This follows DL 57/2008, of March 26th (transposing Directive 2005/29/EC  into Portuguese law), which determines that  that traders must inform users whether the price is personalised based on automated decision-making and profiling of specific consumer behaviour. 
** There is no generic prohibition of discrimination but a prohibition of unjustified geo-blocking and other forms of discrimination based on customers' nationality, place of residence or place of establishment, as per Regulation 2018/302, exists.

{color:#36b37e}CATARINA: In my understanding the test will involve offering the same product under different prices to fully random selection of customers. Hence, the testing is based on randomised selection and, therefore, it appears that we do not have to inform clients of the use of personalised pricing algorithm.{color}

* *UNFAIR PRACTICES*
** Two topics are a matter of concern: price transparency and below-cost sales.
** As regards price transparency, Articles 7(1)(d) and 8(e) of DL 57/2008 deems as unfair (and therefore punishable) any practice capable of somehow inducing the consumer in error as regards the price, its calculation formula or the availability of the product at a given price during a certain period.
** Below-cost prices (i.e. with reference to its effective purchase price which is the invoiced net price minus all payments directly related to the transaction) is prohibited and punished by DL 166/2013. The exceptions for this rule are: (i) perishable goods, as soon as they are threatened with rapid deterioration; (ii) goods whose commercial value is affected, either because the situation that determined their necessity has elapsed, or due to a reduction in their possibilities of use, or due to the supervening of an important technical innovation; (iii) goods whose re-provisioning is done at a lower price, in which case the effective purchase price is replaced by the price resulting from the new purchase invoice; (iv) goods sold in balance or liquidation.

{color:#36b37e}CATARINA: In my understanding the test will not affect or include price transparency and below-cost sales{color}

* *USER DATA COLLECTION*
** Scenario 1 – The data collected through the study is not anonymous and is linked to the user’s personal profile - the GDPR is applicable, meaning that there needs to be legitimate grounds for the processing of the personal data, in this case to carry out the test. The legitimate grounds may be, for example: (i) research and development for app development; (ii) providing better services to the users; (iii) providing access to goods at lower prices. In light of the above, we advise you to check that the processing of user information for this purpose and the relevant legitimate grounds are mentioned in Bolt’s privacy policy, since the users need to be informed.
** Scenario 2 – The data collected through the study is anonymous and it is not linked to the user’s personal profile – The GDPR is not applicable so, therefore there is no need to find a lawful base for the processing of this information.

{color:#36b37e}CATARINA: Could you please confirm the data collected through the study is anonymous?{color}

query to get the sum of the compensation amount in euros

{code:sql}-- driver compensations with grouping by month, country, and types/subtyped if needed
with comp as (
select cda.client_id
	, cda.id
	, ic.external_id 												as driver_id
	, cda.currency 
	, cda.compensation_amount
	, round((cda.compensation_amount / cer.rate), 2)						as compensation_amount_euro
	, cda.compensation_fee_type 
	, cda.compensation_fee_subtype 
	, cda.created 
	, cda.admin_user_id 
	, cda.compensation_comment 
	, date_trunc('month',date(cda.created_date))							as created_month
	, ic.country
from ng_public.etl_billing_compensation_driver_adjustment 	as cda
left join ng_public.invoicing_client 					as ic
	on cda.client_id = ic.id 
	and ic.type = 'Driver'
left join ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates 			as cer
	on cer.currency = cda.currency
	and date(cer.valid_on) = date(cda.created_date)
where 1=1
	and cda.compensation_fee_type not in ('bonus','account_migration')
	and cda.compensation_fee_subtype not in ('fraud_deduction', 'compensation_fuel', 'driver_misconduct', 'ride_overcharge')
	and date(cda.created_date) >= date('2023-05-01')
	and date(cda.created_date) < date ('2023-08-01')
)
select created_month
	, sum(compensation_amount_euro)
from comp
group by 1
order by 1 asc 

-- courier compensations
with comp as (
select cca.invoicing_record_id
	, cca.currency 
	, cca.compensation_amount
	, round((cca.compensation_amount / cer.rate), 2)						as compensation_amount_euro
	, cca.adjustment_type 
	, cca.adjustment_subtype 
	, cca.created 
	, cca.compensation_comment 
	, date_trunc('month',date(cca.created_date))							as created_month
from ng_public.etl_billing_compensation_courier_adjustment 	as cca
left join ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates 			as cer
	on cer.currency = cca.currency
	and date(cer.valid_on) = date(cca.created_date)
where 1=1
	and cca.adjustment_type = 'adjustment'
	and cca.adjustment_subtype in ('delivery_compensation', 'delivery_fee_compensation', 'refund')
	and date(cca.created_date) >= date('2023-05-01')
	and date(cca.created_date) < date ('2023-08-01')
)
with comp as (
select cca.invoicing_record_id
	, cca.currency 
	, cca.compensation_amount
	, round((cca.compensation_amount / cer.rate), 2)						as compensation_amount_euro
	, cca.adjustment_type 
	, cca.adjustment_subtype 
	, cca.created 
	, cca.compensation_comment 
	, date_trunc('month',date(cca.created_date))							as created_month
from ng_public.etl_billing_compensation_courier_adjustment 	as cca
left join ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates 			as cer
	on cer.currency = cca.currency
	and date(cer.valid_on) = date(cca.created_date)
where 1=1
	and cca.adjustment_type = 'adjustment'
	and cca.adjustment_subtype in ('delivery_compensation', 'delivery_fee_compensation', 'refund')
	and date(cca.created_date) >= date('2023-05-01')
	and date(cca.created_date) < date ('2023-08-01')
)
select 
	created_month
	, sum(compensation_amount_euro)			as sum_compensation_amount_eur
from comp
group by 1
order by 1 asc{code}

Hi [~accountid:61124fbaec92ab0070270a0b], regarding your questions above please see my initial thoughts:

* +How do you see this initiative from a reclassification stand point?+ 

As this is a language course, I would not see this as training through which Bolt would be exercising power of direction or determining specific rules to the drivers. However, courts seem to understand that providing training is one of the powers (in addition to orientation, supervision, discipline and monitoring) configuring a relation of subordination between an employee and employer. 

Moreover, It is recommended to never incentive money to a driver directly. {color:#36b37e}_How do you envisage this campaign to be deployed? Will Bolt pay directly the school or the driver? Is this something you have seen being done by competitors in Portugal?_{color}

* +Can we phrase this as a marketing initiative?+ 

{color:#36b37e}_Could you please clarify how would this campaign work differently in such case?_{color} In labour law the analysis of courts are normally factual and therefore I would not see any impact in phrasing it as a marketing initiative, unless this affects the deployment of the campaign.

* +Having absolutely no connection with performance, access to the platform, benefits, etc. what do you believe is the risk of this being used to prove the training criteria?+ 

I believe this is a measure to mitigate risk. The Supreme Court understands that the fact that an individual “receives training and is subject to general guidelines and suggestions … does not in itself mean legal subordination, because in the provision of services, the person who hires can also organize, supervise and monitor their provision with a view to controlling the result.” Hence, *training by itself may not trigger reclassification. The risk is that training combined with other factual situations (real time monitoring of activity and blocking) may trigger and therefore this project would appear to increase the risk of reclassification.*

* +Also considering it is totally optional and it would be for driver who demonstrate interest?+

I believe this is a measure to mitigate risk. Please see previous comment.

As a *conclusion*, I believe that this project would appear to increase the risk of reclassification and would not recommend it, except for the discount available in Bolt Club as other offers already available. Particularly risky would be paying the training directly to the drivers, since invoices is the type of documentation requested in labour inspections.

Please let me know if you have any questions and want to further discuss. We could discuss on our next weekly in more detail. 

Thank you.

Hi,

From a regulatory perspective, I don’t see any safety issues in Romania for the moment. On the contrary, we are being asked by the licensing authority to implement more control on the platform so that drivers will provide quality services. 

In addition, the ride-hailing law in Romania provides that digital platforms must implement a quality control system for the transport activity provided by the alternative transport operators/drivers accepted on the digital platform. “Rating” is what the law has in mind, but I believe the article leaves room for interpretation. 

In terms of reclassification risks, one measure we can take is to inform the fleets (transport operators) that drivers will be subject to prioritisation. In general, it’s ideal to explain to transport operators and drivers what are the conditions. Some explanations on how algorithm works are also welcomed. 

Sorina

The error {{ER_NO_DEFAULT_FOR_FIELD}} simply says that the service is trying to insert a row with a missing value for a column that is not nullable, and has no default value defined in the DB.

This is the correct sequence of operations:

# Add default values to columns.

{noformat}ALTER TABLE taxify_delivery_eta.eta
MODIFY display_delivery_timestamp_seconds INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
MODIFY display_min_delivery_timestamp_seconds INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
MODIFY display_max_delivery_timestamp_seconds INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;{noformat}

2. Wait for the server changes to be released.

3. Drop the columns.

{noformat}ALTER TABLE taxify_delivery_eta.eta
DROP COLUMN display_delivery_timestamp_seconds,
DROP COLUMN display_min_delivery_timestamp_seconds,
DROP COLUMN display_max_delivery_timestamp_seconds;{noformat}

Please let me know when the first alter is done, so I can release the server changes before running the drop.

Hi [~accountid:5d5a47614aeeb80c2cc0d00a] thank you for raising a ticket. 

I have looked into this matter, and it is unclear what constitutes a valid electronic signature in the UK for these kind of agreements. However you mentioned on Slack that this form was sent to the driver via email and the driver filled the form out and emailed back the completed form with his name typed at the bottom as the signature. You have two options here: 

*Option 1:* Provided you have the email thread this would act as ‘proof’ that the driver had the intention to bind himself to this agreement as he has responded to the email attaching the completed form (even though this is a typed signature), so if in the event (worst case scenario) the driver ever disputed not agreeing to this, Bolt would have the email thread which could dispute that argument as we could demonstrate he had the intention to sign.

*Option 2:* If you are in doubt, you could re-send the form to the driver (via HelloSign or Spotdraft) alternatively ask the driver to attend the hub and sign in person in wet ink, if you feel that the driver does not understand the agreement or has signed not knowing what he has signed up for. However, this would be a call you would have to make, taking into account the time and convenience of the driver. 

*To summarise*

This agreement is of low commercial value as it is a commercial being put together of drivers as opposed to a large transaction. It is ultimately up to you and your team to decide on the best approach to take here (option 1 or option 2), it is clear that the driver had the intention to agree to the terms as he has completed the form and sent it back via email. However, if you are in doubt and have any concerns surrounding the drivers intention to agree to the terms and the drivers understanding of the form we would suggest you send the form out again via a different method for signature. 

If you would like to discuss any of the above please do not hesitate to reach out.

Hello Damian Zielinski 

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

h3. {color:#36b37e}*Feedback from TLs*{color}

* *France*: undocumented method to confirm the case & 2x more manual full refunds than auto. 
** The automation rate is low and more manual refunds are issued because the automation is triggered for rides with a 20EUR max fare, and France has more rides with higher fares.
** Undocumented method to confirm the case was misused by OS, they will stop doing that and will follow the process. The market is concerned about the total amount of refunds they make for this issue, so they hope that sticking to the process will decrease the amount of refunds. 
* *UK*: low CSAT & SSAT, low amount of manual refunds, and high amount of auto. 
** Low CSAT: high amount of fraudulent claims where CS doesn’t issue a refund and gets a negative rating.
** Low SSAT: 1. A lot of back and forth with fraudulent customers who are trying to get a refund. 2. Regulation in the UK for riders to confirm their preferred refund method.
** Auto refunds: "Ride did not happen" automation was disabled on 29/05; re-enabled with additional fraud checks on W28. The total refunds dropped 68% from May to July (12.076 to 975).
* *Portugal*: low CSAT & SSAT, high amount of BB refunds. 
** In many cases, riders are unhappy with the refund to BB and reopen the case asking for a refund to the original payment method. That affects negatively the CSAT & SSAT. 
** TL is concerned about the rule to firstly refund to the BB and only if the customer requests, then to the original payment method. She says that the users often refuse BB, and then they get compensated twice (BB and refund to their account).
* *Sweden*: HT 4.6, CSAT, 85.56%, SSAT 77.92%. The market completed [a deep dive|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NOCS/pages/4536697745/Deep+dive+into+the+spike+of+Ride+happened+without+me+cases+during+the+month+of+July+2023] for this issue. Key takeaways:
**  In almost 100% of reviewed cases (when trips are confirmed not to have happened) agents choose to make full refunds to the original payment method (not adhering to the process). And that explains quite high SSAT (in comparison to other markets) and CSAT. 
** In cases where drivers did fraudulent rides, riders would only be more upset for us to offer them credit in the app as compensation for a trip that did not happen through no fault of their own. This would probably only lead to double refunds (one in BB and one to the original payment method) as we are legally bound to provide a refund to the original payment method if a customer asks for one.
* *Poland*: all KPIs are very healthy, what’s their secret? 
** HT & SSAT: Most cases are closed after a first reply - agents check all details in Admin so as to avoid unnecessary back and forths with the customer. This helps keep AHT low and CSAT high (effortless experience for Riders). And it’s not a Quality issue (lack of investigation), as their score is over 90% (Process Adherence included).
** CSAT: A lot of empathetic messages (like "we understand why this is upsetting" and reassurance that we will talk to the driver).
** Overall, effortless experience (fast resolution) and quick information on what will happen to their money are factors the user appreciates.
Relates to Absences and no Financial Impact

[https://community.workday.com/sites/default/files/file-hosting/productionapi/Recruiting/v40.2/Put_Applicant.html|https://community.workday.com/sites/default/files/file-hosting/productionapi/Recruiting/v40.2/Put_Applicant.html|smart-link] 

This is the API that will allow us to create Prehires. I’m assuming we will do all recruiting processes in Greenhouse, not workday. So creating the Prehire is just to ensure the initial data is available.

From that point…

h3. Hire_Employee - Staffing Webservice

[https://community.workday.com/sites/default/files/file-hosting/productionapi/Staffing/v40.2/Hire_Employee.html|https://community.workday.com/sites/default/files/file-hosting/productionapi/Staffing/v40.2/Hire_Employee.html|smart-link] 

This will allow us to create an Employee through a hire process.

* Key requirement is that we know which Prehire to use. So I’m not sure how Greenhouse identifies the correct Prehire, but we’ll need to understand if we can create a report or something similar (Get_Candidates), to allow us to pinpoint the correct prehire to use for the Hire process.
* This “Pre-hire” is still called “*Applicant*” in this WWS, so use that to search. Basically, we need the Prehire object reference ID from somewhere.

h2. Approvals etc

The system can auto-complete both WWS calls, but we need to know if the business wants to maintain the ability to do hire-approvals etc in the Workday system or not.

h1. Greenhouse Data Fields

The data fields that Greenhouse provides are as expected. Of particular interest I find the ability to send Custom Fields. I’m not able to have seen how that works yet within Greenhouse, but it looks like they allow user admins to create custom fields (kind of like Telema dimensions) that can be sent over. So if there is every a particular thing we want to have sent over, we can use that, if it’s not on the standard process.

Greenhouse makes the following webhooks available that we would _particularly_ care about:

* Application Created
** This is for new application creations = Put_Applicant WWS
* Candidate Hired
** As expected, this would trigger the > Hire_Employee WWS
* Candidate/Prospect rejected
** This would require an update on our end to deactivate the prehire with Rejected status.
** One concern I have is that in Greenhouse you can ‘unreject’ someone. I haven’t seen how it works in Workday in regards to a rejected prehire… whether it goes away entirely or not.
* Candidate anonymized
** This is a GDPR piece, which means that if the Candidate requests Greenhouse to make them anonymous, they must comply. And we must as well. *I think this might cause issues with compliance vs working processes.*

I’m not sure if we want to be updating through the webhook EVERY time someone updates their data in Greenhouse, as they do not seem to have a limit on the number of updates they can send.

Another thing that concerns me is why or how Greenhouse would use the “Merge Applicant” process. And how that reflects on our business. We would need to deactivate one of the two prehires. The reason for that is because Greenhouse provides unique ids to each applicant profile, which would trigger the Application Created event, thus forcing us to create a new Prehire.
